ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to RydeHELP human review: route-deviation money claim (0.77 km unexempt segment, $1.09) held pending review of the threat-tagged chat message; reviewer to confirm whether the keyword hit is a false positive, then apply RD-1/RD-2.
ruling.escalation_reason: Chat fact F7 / F8 contains a [threat]-tagged rider message with threat keywords detected; SAFE-1 requires escalation to a human reviewer instead of an automatic ruling.

segment_findings.reason: Single off-route segment 09:49–09:52 adding 0.77 km, up to 1019 m off the optimal route; RD-3(a) has no rider-named stop [F7], RD-4 fails because there is no traffic incident [F12] and only band 4 readings [F10][F11], and RD-5 fails because the driver's GPS-following admission [F9] shows no pre-departure rider consent — so the segment is unexempt under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted only in part and subsumed by escalation: the meter-based excess is real on the system record [F1][F6], but the billed $2.30 full excess [F4] is capped by the single unexempt segment under RD-2 and no ruling is issued while the threat tag stands [F8].
The $1.09 figure is arithmetically sound (0.77 km × $1.41/km [F3][F4][F6]) but no refund is ordered: the settled SAFE-1 tag [F8] directs escalate, and the amount is held for the human reviewer.
The driver's attempt to shelter the deviation behind the rider's lobby message fails: that message names no stop or route, so RD-3(a) gives no cover, as the driver's own brief concedes [F7].
The driver's failure to establish RD-4 must cut against him, not cap liability at one segment: the consequence of a failed RD-4 defence is RD-2 treatment of the unexempt segment [F10][F11][F12].

The contention that 'find you at the lobby' [F7] is innocuous and that no escalation arises cannot stand against the settled threat-keyword finding [F8]; SAFE-1 puts the safety question to a human reviewer, not to the advocates.
